name: Inner join
description: Combines rows of two tables that match on a condition; unmatched rows disappear.

name: Row multiplication
description: A join returns one row per matching pair, so the result can have more rows than either table.

name: Query execution order
description: A query runs FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY, LIMIT, which is not the order it is written in.

name: Alias scope
description: A column alias made in SELECT exists only in the stages after SELECT, so WHERE cannot use it but ORDER BY can.

name: Row order is not guaranteed
description: A table has no inherent row order; without ORDER BY, LIMIT returns some rows, not the first ones.

name: Three-valued logic
description: A comparison with NULL is neither true nor false but unknown, and AND, OR and NOT follow a truth table with three values.

name: IS NULL test
description: IS NULL and IS NOT NULL are the only comparisons that answer true or false for NULL.

name: WHERE drops unknown rows
description: WHERE keeps only rows where the condition is true, so rows with an unknown result disappear, including for <>.

name: GROUP BY buckets
description: GROUP BY puts rows into buckets by key and collapses each bucket into one row; it does not promise any order.

name: Aggregate functions
description: count, sum, avg, min and max turn the many rows of a bucket into one value.

name: HAVING versus WHERE
description: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters buckets after aggregation.

name: count(*) versus count(column)
description: count(*) counts rows; count(column) counts rows where that column is not NULL.

name: Column types
description: The type of a column decides which values are stored, compared and sorted, for example text, integer, numeric, timestamptz and boolean.

name: Money as numeric
description: Exact amounts use numeric or integer cents, because floating point types cannot store most decimal fractions exactly.

name: Primary key
description: A primary key is a column or set of columns that is unique and not NULL and identifies exactly one row.

name: Column constraints
description: NOT NULL, UNIQUE and CHECK let the database refuse bad data no matter which application wrote it.

name: Foreign key
description: A foreign key makes the database refuse a value that points to a row that does not exist.

name: One-to-many relation
description: The foreign key lives on the many side: each order row points to one customer, a customer has many orders.

name: Junction table
description: A many-to-many relation needs a third table with one foreign key to each side, usually with a composite primary key.

name: Referential actions
description: ON DELETE decides what happens to child rows when a parent row is deleted; the default refuses the delete.

name: Left join
description: A left join keeps every row of the left table and fills the right side with NULL when nothing matches.

name: Filtering a left join
description: A WHERE condition on a right-table column removes the NULL-filled rows and turns a left join into an inner join; the condition belongs in ON.

name: Update and delete anomalies
description: Facts stored in several rows can drift apart on update, and deleting a row can destroy an unrelated fact.

name: Normalization
description: Each fact lives in exactly one place, so one change touches one row.

name: Denormalization trade-off
description: Copying data on purpose can speed up reads, but it makes the copies your job to keep in sync.

name: Sequential scan
description: Without a usable index the database reads every row of the table, so the cost grows with table size.

name: B-tree index
description: A B-tree index keeps values sorted in a tree, so finding one value takes a few steps instead of a full scan.

name: Execution plan
description: EXPLAIN shows the plan the planner chose and its estimated costs; EXPLAIN ANALYZE also runs the query and shows real times.

name: Index write cost
description: Every index must be updated on each insert, update and delete of an indexed value, and it takes disk space.

name: Planner choice
description: The planner picks the cheapest plan it estimates, so it may ignore an index on a tiny table or a query that matches most rows.

name: Transaction
description: BEGIN to COMMIT groups statements so they succeed together or, after ROLLBACK, not at all.

name: Lost update
description: Two sessions that read a value, compute and write it back can overwrite each other, so money or stock vanishes.

name: Read committed isolation
description: In PostgreSQL default isolation a statement sees only committed data, but two statements in one transaction can see different data.

name: Row lock
description: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE or an UPDATE locks the row until the transaction ends, so other writers wait instead of overwriting.

name: Deadlock
description: Two transactions each hold a lock the other needs; PostgreSQL detects the cycle and aborts one of them with an error.

name: Consistent lock order
description: If every transaction takes locks in the same order, a cycle cannot form.
